Section: IN-TOOLS #361-A — opt-in metered physical Liquid Drain > Reproducing the focused checks
Use the pinned, source-matched native and Rapier runtimes and the repository's Godot version. The three `test_physical_metered_*.gd` files are discovered by the existing Godot regression route. A direct focused run uses: ```sh godot --headless --path godot --editor --import godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_physical_metered_drain.gd godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_physical_metered_equipment.gd godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_physical_metered_desktop.gd python3 tools/lcb/run_metered_drain_native.py --output-dir build/metered-drain-native-run python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/lcb -p test_metered_drain_native.py -v ``` The native runner requires a **new** output directory, compiles the source, seals source/compiler/executable identity and validates a complete typed result census. It is a standalone scoped control command, not an additional registered hosted Native job. Native-only controls cannot establish actor input or Rapier safety. Headless Main plus injected input events cannot establish graphical pacing, physical mouse/keyboard operation, Windows execution or owner handling feel. Controlled quantity arms disable reactions and unrelated sources/edits and check `initial + admitted sources - explicit sinks = remaining stored quantity` after accepted operations and drain shutoff. Water units and Brine populations remain separate. Wall positions, forbidden-side cells and actual native masks accompany quantity totals. Command-owner timing and native tick timing are separate; configured worker count is accompanied by observed native phase claimants. Each of the eight registered large standalone native four-worker arms must observe exactly four distinct phase claimants, with exactly one in its one-worker control. The smaller 312-cell Godot fixture intentionally observes at most two claimants with four configured workers; it is a separate application proof host. The result's `read_accounting = material-work-units-v1` names the narrower historical contract. `reads_used` charges each actual `inspect_cell` preflight or post-write call once, plus conservative helper identity reservations: ten units for refresh/tick/revision setup, six for the pre-write identity check and eight for final identity/tick/revision readback. Cached preflight cells are reused; post-write inspections are fresh and charged separately. Short-circuit refusals may use fewer native calls than their reserved units. Writes have their own capacity and are not counted as reads. The shared runtime adds every existing source-clearance material/body-mask read and each optional observation read. Repeated source-mask reads remain separate charged calls; they are not silently deduplicated. Optional 81-cell patches run only when all 81 read units remain. Before the first erase, the helper retains capacity for every intended post-readback and both required identity checks; insufficient capacity refuses the entire effect without an attempted write. Section: IN-TOOLS #361-A — opt-in metered physical Liquid Drain > Implementation and acceptance boundary
**Current candidate source:** `metered-drain-v1` adds exact quantity accounting to the existing physical U10 `liquid_drain`. It uses the existing equipment, physical actor session, worker admission and native World. Ordinary U10 remains the default. Sampled usables, material IDs, production solver defaults, native movement laws, the adapter ABI and Rapier coupling are unchanged. The [dated qualification record](../audits/2026-11-04-in-tools-361a-metered-drain.md) separates native primitive controls, actual Godot/worker execution, synthetic desktop input and untested platform/human acceptance. This candidate does not claim full #361-A acceptance until its remaining gates pass. Parent [#361](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/361) stays open. The [successor correction and fresh qualification](../audits/2026-11-04-in-tools-383-successor-correction.md) records A01's exact four-claimant admission and A02's explicitly limited material-work contract at measured implementation `e11b452f`. Earlier `f4878302`/`73b10f9b` and frozen independent `c83984c0` results retain their own historical source identities. PR #383 remains Draft. Planning authority is [#379 at `24d0e612`](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/24d0e612ae986edbdc48e5b94f52315d9c3d8421/docs/architecture/in-tools-gameplay-admission.md), including its `in-tools.usable-liquid-drain.v1` registration. This implementation does not require merging that preparation branch. The executable [physical fixture v1](../../godot/tests/fixtures/in-tools-metered-drain.v1.json) registers its own geometry and measured quantities; it does not relabel the planned #379 tank or #370 comparison recorder as executed.

Section: IN-TOOLS #361-A — opt-in metered physical Liquid Drain > Ownership, observations and failure semantics
[`physical_usable_runtime.gd`](../../godot/scripts/physical_usable_runtime.gd) calls the owner-local [`metered_liquid_drain.gd`](../../godot/scripts/metered_liquid_drain.gd) helper only inside the existing worker consumption interval. The cancellation mutex linearizes admission and the entire finite operation. Main supplies copied equipment/body values; the worker prepares native masks from its captured physical frame before consumption. No main-thread World writer, global state or additional queue is introduced. The version-2 request extends the ordinary request with `profile`, `material`, `native_generation`, `policy_hash`, `world_instance_id` and `quantity_budget`. The physical frame echoes these values plus the current `metered_request_id`. Release retires that token immediately; latest held-state admission prevents a quick press/release from reappearing through the ordinary edge replay. Existing run/epoch, control generation, equipment epoch/instance, body, strictly increasing sequence and lease checks still apply. Native ObjectIDs are signed opaque values; nonzero identity, rather than positivity, is required. All destructive preflight finishes before the first writer: equipment identity, owner policy and health, finite positive bounds, charge/cooldown, full selected target quantities, body masks, visibility, adapter bounds and reserved read/write capacity. The helper uses `CyberDemoBridge.inspect_cell` for **stored** material, quantity and mask state, then the existing radius-zero Empty edit. A void writer or unchanged health flag is never counted as success. Every attempted edit has copied native post-readback; positive totals come only from verified transitions. Results are labelled **`host-local-native-observation-v1`**. They bind the command and captured frame to native World object/generation, applied policy, completed native tick and hard-surface revision. Initial native construction receipts remain separately labelled; IN admission checks their canonical byte hash. They are not per-command native receipts. The adapter exposes no separate native pose revision: the result says so and records the captured physical-frame/mask provenance instead. Whole-World censuses in the fixtures independently check the local transition ledger; production does not run a full-World scan for every pulse. A **normal refusal** performs no destructive edit, consumes no effect allowance, charges no activation cost and starts no new cooldown. Ordinary simulation time may still recharge charge and age an existing cooldown. A command consumed as refused cannot later retry because its intake becomes clear. Admission-only refusals are labelled `not_dispatched`; they do not fabricate an inspected target set or fresh native per-command receipt. An **unexpected execution fault** is distinct. The helper latches terminal *before* the first writer. It retains attempted transitions, verified partial quantity and whether quantity verification is complete. The worker then pauses, retires pending effects/brush commands and publishes failure evidence alongside the last valid render/cell publication. It cannot continue a native tick, retry the command or publish partial cells as a healthy frame. Restart preserves that quarantine while allowing an explicit existing clear/prepared reconstruction. Section: Interfaces and message contracts > Physical actor control and effects > Metered U10 request and outcome extension
The opt-in [#361-A profile](../operations/in-tools-metered-drain.md) uses request version 2 and adds exactly `profile="metered-drain-v1"`, selected `material` (Water 3 or Brine 24), `native_generation`, `policy_hash`, `world_instance_id` and integer `quantity_budget`. The physical frame remains version 1; its metered actor row echoes those fields and the current `metered_request_id`. No arbitrary target position, footprint, writer or velocity enters the request. Signed nonzero native ObjectIDs are opaque identity values. A current profile refuses a version-1 downgrade and a retired pending token cannot dispatch. Each actor readback adds copied `metered_drain` owner context and separate `water_units_{initial,remaining,removed}` and `brine_cells_{initial,remaining,removed}` ledgers. Command results add `metered_drain.status` (`applied`, `refused`, `fault`), reason, requested budget, applied policy, before/after completed tick, target observations/transitions, actual quantity, sink debit, remaining allowance and charge/cooldown outcome. Results carry `provenance="host-local-native-observation-v1"`; an initial native construction receipt is separately labelled. No native per-command receipt or unexposed native pose revision is claimed. Admission-only refusals say `observation_status="not_dispatched"` rather than inventing inspected targets. `read_accounting="material-work-units-v1"` qualifies `reads_used`: helper cell inspections plus reserved helper identity work, within the shared material-work allowance. Caller lifecycle refresh and mask preparation are outside that counter; it is not an all-native-getter limit. The [profile accounting contract](../operations/in-tools-metered-drain.md#reproducing-the-focused-checks) defines the counted work and pre-write reservations. `metered_terminal` and `metered_fault` expose an unexpected execution fault. Verified partial quantities remain evidence, while uncertain quantity is marked incomplete. Faulted owners stop editing/ticking and publish failure with the last valid cellular/render frame until explicit native reconstruction. Normal refusals have zero removal, zero new allowance debit and no accepted activation. The ordinary request/result fields and sampled equipment interface remain intact.
